subject: Clarify: backup retention, regional deletion propagation, and legal-hold overlap
messages:
From: Kim Sanders <kim.sanders@helioshealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Lopez <david.lopez@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on backup deletion propagation and legal hold overlap

Hi Rafael,

Quick follow-up from our compliance review — thanks again for the demo. Two questions came up that our security team wants clarified before we proceed with a PoC:

1) If an end-user record is deleted in the application, how long until that object is removed from offsite backups (cross-region snapshots)? We need to understand the full window where PII could still exist in backups.

2) If we place a legal hold for a specific customer (retention override), does that prevent snapshot tombstone sweep/expunge across replicas or only on the primary copy?

We have a tight audit timeline and would also appreciate an example timeline for: user delete -> tombstone created -> snapshot sweep -> expunge.

Thanks — Kim
Kim Sanders
Director, Security & Compliance
Helios Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Sanders <kim.sanders@helioshealth.com>
Cc: David Lopez <david.lopez@helioshealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on backup deletion propagation and legal hold overlap

Hi Kim — thanks for these precise questions. Looping in Marissa (DR/ops) and Aditya (security engineering) so we can give you a concise timeline and the caveats. Attaching a short policy extract and a cross-region retention map to illustrate.

Short answers up front:
- Default backup retention for hosted snapshots is 45 days; cross-region replicas inherit the same TTL but have an eventual-expunge window that can vary by region (typically +24-72 hours).
- Legal hold (retention override) applies at the customer account level in our control plane and prevents automated tombstone expunge across all replicas for the scope of the hold. It does not make the data visible in customer-facing restore operations unless explicitly requested for an investigation.

We should still provide a step-by-step timeline; Marissa, can you paste the typical flow and any exceptions?

— Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Sanders <kim.sanders@helioshealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on backup deletion propagation and legal hold overlap

Hi Kim — adding the operational timeline and some edge cases. Pasting the concise flow below; I left the excerpts from our runbook at the bottom.

Operational timeline (standard hosted configuration):
- T0 (user deletes record): application marks row as deleted and issues a logical delete request to the store; an internal tombstone marker is created immediately.
- T0+1min–30min: Tombstone is replicated to primary replica set and written to the write-ahead log.
- T0+4–12h: Automated incremental snapshot includes the tombstone marker (depends on snapshot cadence — we default to 6hr incremental).
- Snapshot retention window: 45 days by default. Snapshots older than 45 days are tombstoned at snapshot index and queued for sweep.
- Sweep/expunge window: once a snapshot is eligible, expunge jobs run per-region. There are three phases: mark-for-expunge -> soft-expunge (objects unlinked) -> hard-expunge (objects garbage-collected from object-store). Typical per-region delay between mark and hard-expunge is 24–72 hours due to consistency/replication checks and retention indexing.

Implications for your questions:
- Effective exposure window after delete: worst-case = snapshot cadence (6hr) + remaining retention on captured snapshot (up to 45 days) + per-region expunge delay (up to 72 hours). So, from an audit perspective you should assume up to ~45 days + small operational skew.
- Legal hold/retention override: when a customer-level hold is applied in our control plane, expunge jobs skip matching objects across all replicas. That hold is durable until removed (manual or via API) and is tracked in our retention index.

Edge cases and notes:
- If a customer is using Dedicated or Private deployment, retention defaults can differ (we can set policy to 90 days or custom values) and the expunge orchestration is run in-customer-region which may increase or decrease sweep windows.
- If KMS key rotation or destruction is requested, that affects the ability to decrypt older snapshots; key destruction is a separate legal/contractual process and would be handled with an explicit key-destruction request.
- For emergency expunge (e.g., right-to-be-forgotten legal orders), we have an SLA path — we’ll treat those as manual operations and they require account-owner sign-off and audit logs.

Marissa Cole
Director, Disaster Recovery Operations
Redwood Inference

--- Excerpt from runbook (simplified) ---
Mark-for-expunge -> soft-expunge -> hard-expunge; per-region job queueing; cross-region consistency window added to avoid split-brain deletions; legal-hold flag prevents mark-for-expunge stage.

Subject: Re: Questions on backup deletion propagation and legal hold overlap

Thanks — that helps a lot. Two follow-ups: 1) Can you confirm whether the 45-day default includes both incremental and full snapshots (i.e., are fulls kept longer?), and 2) For legal hold we need proof of cross-region hold behavior for our auditors — can you provide an immutable log extract or retention-index snapshot that shows the hold applied across replicas?

If you can provide a sample audit extract (redacted) and clarify full vs incremental retention, we can move this into our procurement checklist.

— Kim
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Sanders <kim.sanders@helioshealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on backup deletion propagation and legal hold overlap

Hi Kim — quick follow-up from security eng.

1) Retention semantics: 45 days applies to snapshot objects (both incremental deltas and full snapshots). We keep a chain such that full+incrementals are logically retained for the configured TTL. There is no separate longer retention for fulls by default. In Dedicated/Private we can customize this and keep archival fulls longer if requested.

2) Audit evidence: we can produce a redacted retention-index extract showing the legal-hold flag as a time-stamped entry and the corresponding replica IDs. We typically deliver this as an exportable JSON/CSV with signatures from our audit log (append-only). I’ve attached a redacted example and will schedule a short proofing call to walk through the fields.

Action items:
- Rafael: schedule 30-min call this week to deliver the extract and answer procurement questions.
- Marissa: prepare redacted retention-index extract (include replica IDs and timestamps).

Thanks — Aditya
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
